title: FlowTrace lifecycle: agent-authored walkthrough to Neovim navigation

node-1.label: Agent researches the requested code flow
node-1.summary: The skill tells the calling coding agent to inspect the repository and build understanding itself. FlowTrace is the artifact format, validator, terminal previewer, and Neovim viewer.

node-2.label: CLI entrypoint dispatches helper commands
node-2.summary: The Go CLI dispatches build, context, validate, and print. The context/build commands are deterministic helpers; they do not call an LLM.

node-3.label: Agent writes the final .flow.json artifact
node-3.summary: A FlowTrace artifact is a schemaVersion, root node id, and node map. Nodes point at real files and can include stable anchors/symbols for jump-time resolution.

node-4.label: build/context collect deterministic candidate snippets
node-4.summary: Build derives search terms, scans source files, formats snippets, and either prints context or emits a search-based scaffold. This is a helper for the agent, not the source of truth.

node-5.label: validate checks references before the user opens the artifact
node-5.summary: Validation checks required top-level fields, node ids, file existence, line ranges, resolution values, and child/branch targets.

node-6.label: print renders a terminal preview
node-6.summary: The print command walks the root node, recursively renders child and branch targets, and helps catch shape issues before opening Neovim.

node-7.label: :FlowTraceOpen loads the artifact in Neovim
node-7.summary: The Neovim command calls M.open, which loads JSON, creates the FlowTrace pane, installs keymaps, and redraws the tree.

node-8.label: parser.load decodes and sanity-checks JSON
node-8.summary: The parser reads the file, decodes JSON with vim.json.decode, and ensures root and nodes are present before rendering.

node-9.label: tree.render flattens nodes into a readable buffer
node-9.summary: Rendering builds title/help rows, label/meta/file/summary rows for each node, highlight spans, and a row-to-node index for actions.

node-10.label: jump resolves anchors at navigation time
node-10.summary: When the user presses <CR>, the plugin opens the target file in a code window and resolves anchor, then symbol, then stored line number. This keeps jumps useful after nearby edits move code.
